g.title: P0
g.text: attester TPM :2321 · RP TPM :2325 — separate NVChip dirs,
each given its own TPM2_Startup(CLEAR). Separate seeds, so the
two AKs are unrelated by construction.

g.title: P1
g.text: --role attester against the attester TPM → AK_a public half
--role relying-party against the RP TPM → AK_r public half
: without it each run emits BOTH
identities, putting a key the RP's own TPM can derive into the

g.title: S2
g.text: RP picks a nonce and a PCR selection

g.title: TM
g.text: resolves IDs to host:port from verifiers_config.txt.

g.title: S3
g.text: ① AK_a in the trust anchor ② Quote_a signature ③ nonce
④ log entries self-consistent ⑥ file hashes vs whitelist/blacklist
compare against Quote_a's PCR digest. Software because the RP is
checking someone else's claim, not making one.
replay: different log, different purpose, different machine.
All six run even after one fails, so one pass reports everything.

g.title: ATT
g.text: Extends its real IMA log into PCR 10, then TPM2_Quote over
— its TPM's RESTRICTED primary, the only
kind whose signature proves the TPM built the structure.
Returns Quote_a + log_a + AK_a's public half.

g.title: S4
g.text: charra_sdk_redact_ima_log() rewrites each entry's PATH only.
Randomised, so it is done ONCE per cycle — per Verifier would
hand each of them a different log_r for the same attestation.

g.title: S5
g.text: 5 · replay log_r into PCR 23, on the RP's TPM
TPM2_PCR_Reset(23), then one TPM2_PCR_Extend per entry.
Once per cycle, not per Verifier
consuming it, so one replay backs every quote below.
PCR 23 because it is resettable from locality 0 and PCR 10 is not,
and because it is outside the Attester's quoted selection.

g.title: Q
g.text: is the RP still qualified at this point?
need only be valid HERE, not for the whole round that follows. One
that lapses mid-round costs that cycle — every Verifier votes NO and
/appraise never says why. The next cycle re-qualifies and it corrects.
no → qualify first (step 6) · yes → straight to step 7

g.title: S6
g.text: Redact the Verifier's synthetic challenge log with the SDK and
compares log bytes, and identical logs replay identically.
The signature says WHO submitted; the salt binds it to THIS challenge.

g.title: S7
g.text: → POST /appraise. One quote each, over the one shared replay.

g.title: VQ
g.text: Fabricates a synthetic log, redacts it itself for the golden answer,
sends the raw log + salt. On submit: AK_r in the anchor, signature
over (log ‖ salt) valid, and the RP's redaction equal to the golden
one BYTE FOR BYTE. Records SHA-256(AK_r) + deadline in
, shared by every Verifier, and returns that

g.title: S8
g.text: fail-closed: a Verifier counts as a pass only if it appraised AND
accepted. Unreachable, timed out, or never sent all count as NO.

g.title: VA
g.text: ① AK_r in the trust anchor
①b this RP qualified, per the shared file
③ nonce, read from the quote's
[Verifier as CHECKER — it opens no TPM at all]
① AK_a in the anchor ② Quote_a signature ③ nonce
Opens NO TPM: every check is public-key math or hashing.
③ and ④ together are what bind the log to a TPM-attested value.
The verdict on the wire is a bare pass/fail — the RP is never told
WHICH check failed. Reasons go to the Verifier's log only.

g.title: ABORT
g.text: Not fatal to the daemon: the next cycle starts fresh. The RP does not
retry within a cycle -- a briefly unreachable peer costs one cycle.
